question.:question/problem: What is the slope of the tangent line to the curve $y=16x-40cos⁡x$ at the point $x=\frac{\pi }{6}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The slope at $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$ is given by the value of the derivative ${y}^{′}$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{6}.$ 

First, we compute the derivative, using the fact that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(cos⁡x)=-sin⁡x.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(16x-40cos⁡x) \\  & =16-40(-sin⁡x) \\  & =16+40sin⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=\frac{\pi }{6},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =16+40sin⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =16+40(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =16+\frac{40}{2} \\  & =\frac{72}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,  the instantaneous rate of change is $\frac{72}{2}.$

question.:question/problem: What is the slope of the tangent line to the curve $y=22x-55cos⁡x$ at the point $x=\frac{\pi }{6}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The slope at $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$ is given by the value of the derivative ${y}^{′}$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{6}.$ 

First, we compute the derivative, using the fact that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(cos⁡x)=-sin⁡x.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(22x-55cos⁡x) \\  & =22-55(-sin⁡x) \\  & =22+55sin⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=\frac{\pi }{6},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6}) & =22+55sin⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =22+55(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =22+\frac{55}{2} \\  & =\frac{99}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,  the instantaneous rate of change is $\frac{99}{2}.$
